1	## Review scope protocol
2	
3	Reviewers need task status alongside the diff and design docs. Without scope, they flag code-that-isn't-written-yet as `MISSING_IMPL` (spec review) or as missing functionality (code review). Standard review uses this scope locally; isolated review injects the same artifact into sub-agent and external-reviewer prompts. The existing /kk:review-spec payload remains sufficient; no additional change-context record is required by this protocol.
4	
5	**Code-review timing:** apply this protocol's task-document reads during the
6	post-instruction investigation phase, after every resolved checklist is loaded.
7	Early diff selection uses filenames and Git metadata; it is distinct from
8	determining task scope. Reading this protocol does not authorize early inspection
9	of a discovered task file's requirements. The calling workflow still governs
10	any bounded inspection needed solely for a declared routing predicate.
11	
12	### Input shapes
13	
14	The review workflow must handle three invocation shapes:
15	
16	1. **Invoked from `/kk:implement`** — `/docs/feat/wip/[feature]/` exists with `design.md`, `implementation.md`, `tasks.md`. The current task id is known (the one just finished). Use full scope filtering.
17	2. **Invoked directly inside a feature** — `/docs/feat/wip/[feature]/` exists but no current task is explicitly supplied. Derive scope from `tasks.md` status fields (`done` = in scope, `pending`/`in-progress` = out of scope).
18	3. **Invoked on an arbitrary diff** — no `/docs/feat/wip/` directory relates to the diff. Skip the scope artifact entirely and note "No task scope available" in the reviewer prompt.
19	
20	### Scope artifact format
21	
22	When shape 1 or 2 applies, build this block and inject it into every reviewer prompt (sub-agent prompt template and the external-reviewer `step` framing):
23	
24	```
25	## Task Scope
26	
27	Review mode: {mid-implementation | post-implementation}
28	
29	In scope (review these):
30	- Task {id}: {title} — status: done
31	- [...more done tasks if applicable]
32	
33	Out of scope (pending — DO NOT flag as missing):
34	- Task {id}: {title} — status: {pending|in-progress}
35	- [...more pending tasks]
36	
37	The feature's design docs describe the full end state. Pending tasks are expected gaps in the current diff — treat their absence from the code as intentional, not as a finding. You may still flag issues within the in-scope tasks even if they reference pending tasks (e.g., a broken interface contract). Pending work does not excuse current regressions or incompatibility: assess whether the reviewed increment preserves existing flows and meets applicable delivery requirements. Genuinely unreachable unfinished paths need not be implemented merely because they are planned.
38	```
39	
40	When shape 3 applies, use:
41	
42	```
43	## Task Scope
44	
45	No task scope available — review the diff on its own merits without assuming any feature-level design doc.
46	```
47	
48	### Determining mode
49	
50	- **mid-implementation** — at least one task in `tasks.md` has status `pending` or `in-progress`.
51	- **post-implementation** — all tasks are `done`.
52	
53	In shape 1, the invoking workflow (`/kk:implement`) may pass the current task id directly; that task is automatically in scope even if `tasks.md` hasn't been updated yet.
54	
55	### Interpretation guidance for reviewers
56	
57	The reviewer prompt must also carry this instruction (agent definitions should state it; the workflow relays it implicitly via the scope block):
58	
59	- Do **not** report missing-implementation findings for items covered only by out-of-scope tasks.
60	- Do still report real issues *within* the in-scope tasks, including ones that affect future pending work (e.g., a public API the pending task will depend on is shaped wrongly).
61	- A current consumer that already requires a pending provider change remains reviewable, including when the larger feature is disabled. Distinguish deployment from activation and check the actual affected paths; a flag or a future task alone proves neither reachability nor safety.
62	- Attribute introduced/worsened behavior separately from inherited defects. Do not invent a current regression or require pending work when the increment remains compatible under its actual delivery contract.
63	- If a finding would be valid *only* after pending work lands, mention it under "Areas Not Covered" instead of the P0–P3 sections.
64
